decisive_items: acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to their left arm
ECG showed a sinus rhythm at a rate of 85 beats/min with the presence of broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5
Subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery
response.rationale: The only candidate is strongly supported by the raw vignette: typical anginal chest pain, ECG showing hyperacute T waves, and coronary angiography confirming subtotal LAD occlusion. The normal troponin is not contradictory as it can be negative early in ACS. No other candidates were provided.
